chapter: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
title: Johnny's loss of sight, the 1932 bus accident and the Braille Institute
summary: Johnny's partial sight ended when a bus hit him in 1932; he died in 1955 and his machine went to the Braille Institute.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Johnny was how old when he lost his sight?
Well, he was... That was '55, and I was... be 67, wouldn't I? 'Cause I was born in '88, and he was seven years older 'n me, so he'd've been sixty-uh...he'd've been 74.
And the operation that...that completely took his sight--that was...

Well, I told you that he could see a little bit... uh...but I told you that it wasn't so smart those days. They had... he could see through like that...so, just chipped a piece outa there, and they couldn't save this eye at all, and that way it went on for years, and he...it cut him down at night. He never did hardly go nowhere at night unless it somebody...I went with him, somebody'd taken his arm. And in '32, he was getting off a streetcar, where we lived,
at Denker there, and Jefferson, and he went to go 'round the street-car, and another one...bus hit him. Knocked him clear up over the sidewalk, and after that, he never did see any more.
Did you say that this invention he came up with is still used at the Braille Institute?

I think so. Yeah, because my sister-in-law has only been dead about five years, and she handled it, and when she died, she gave them all her money. She had thirty, forty thousand dollars, and she gave it to the Braille...because he was blind. I guess it was in sympathy with him, you know, and she gave them all of the apparatus and everything. It all went to the Braille in the will.
That was something valuable, and obviously, he used it. Right? Himself.

Yeah, what little writing he did, he used it. But they had him on the air--on television...I think, television... and two or three times with his machine. Yeah. But he had inventive ideas, you know. He was a real musician, you know. He was dedicated to that, so, it took up all of his ideas on that.
